title: LIMIT: the database's 'just the first few'

steps.title: Top 3 heavyweights
steps.prompt:
LIMIT chops the result after N rows - like asking the librarian to start at the top and only read the first three cards.
Combine it with ORDER BY … DESC to get the three most expensive products:
steps.task: Fill the blank: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT ___;
hints: We want the heavyweights - the priciest.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3;
steps.seed_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT ___;
steps.memory_trick: LIMIT cuts the list after N rows.

steps.title: Run it for real
steps.prompt: Now type the whole thing yourself, no blank this time.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3;
hints: Start with SELECT name, price FROM products.
Finish with LIMIT and a number.
Write LIMIT 3 at the very end.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 3;
steps.memory_trick: Bottom line of the query = how many rows you keep.

steps.title: A quick peek
steps.prompt:
LIMIT is brilliant for a quick look at strange tables: 'just show me a sample.'
You type * to get all columns, then LIMIT 5 to only take five rows.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT * FROM products LIMIT 5;
steps.memory_trick: SELECT * + LIMIT = a quick sample, fast to read.

steps.title: Predict the row count
steps.task: How many rows does the result show?
hints: Look at the last word of the query.
The number after LIMIT is the answer.
steps.memory_trick: The number after LIMIT is your row count.
